title: SOS POST cancel path has no rate limiting; spec 18.4.1 rate table covers all SOS types
description: Found by security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-r7hs (P3). python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py _cancel_from_body (:277-308) calls neither evaluate_rate_limit nor _record_request, while the activate path does (evaluate :263, 4.29+retry_after :265-271, record :273). spec/12-apps.md:560-573 (18.4.1) defines the per-source SOS rate table (600s cooldown, 3/hour, burst 2) for SOS messages generally, and 18.4.2 (:597-619) classifies cancel as an SOS type - so cancel is currently a spec deviation. Mitigations verified: when idle the handler short-circuits 4.04 before any parsing (:283-284); when active, bounded CBOR decode (4096B/1024 items/depth 16) + envelope shape checks + _pubkey_to_iid sha512 all run BEFORE the Schnorr48 verify, so garbage floods are cheap and there is no unbounded-work or memory-growth path (cancel never touches _request_times; ikcx leak is activate-side). Residual impact: unthrottled response generation (one 4.01/4.04 per request) and spec non-compliance. Fix: either apply the same evaluate_rate_limit/_record_request pair keyed by the active origin's source_key (but keep legitimate cancel un-blockable - e.g. exempt the valid-originator cancel from the budget while still recording it), or add a cheap pre-filter counter; decide semantics, then mirror in render_delete (which is likewise unthrottled) and pin with a test asserting rate-budget neutrality for a valid cancel (overlaps snh1's neutrality assertion - coordinate).
